newsitem.title: UK: Tomkins results top forecasts, outlook good.
newsitem.headline: Tomkins results top forecasts, outlook good.

text.p: Tomkins Plc, the British baking- to-engineering conglomerate, saw half-year pretax profits top analysts' forecasts at 168.8 million pounds ($283.7 million) on Monday and reported an encouraging outlook for the second half.
Profits were up 34 percent from the previous year and the interim dividend payout was in line with expectations at three pence per share versus 2.7 pence.
Gregory Hutchings, executive chairman said in the interim statement "It is pleasing to report another period of outperformance for Tomkins."
The chairman said most of the group's divisions had turned in profits ahead of the preceding year.

Commenting on the outlook for the rest of the year, he said: "Prospects for the second half look encouraging, with the majority of our operations having healthy order books and satisfactory market conditions. We are delighted with the purchase of Gates (Corp for $1.1 billion last year) which has proved entirely consistent with our expectations."
Excluding currency effects, organic growth in operating profit was up more than 10 percent on sales which rose seven percent.

Last week's speculation of a possible share buyback failed to be realised. Net cash rose to 366.8 million at the end of the six month period to November 2, after accounting for Gates' debt of 129.7 million. ($1=.5950 Pound)
